items.title: Don Alias interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002
items.q: And my dad, he separated and divorced like early on when we were young

ctx.x: What did your parents do for a living?

Mom was a supervisor at Harlem Hospital, which was like right down the street. Grandmom was a head caterer in the kitchen. And the one thing I can always remember about that is around Thanksgiving and Christmas we’d get this phone call and she’d be working and she’d say “come now” and we’d run over there and she’d have like — because they were going to throw it away anyway, all this surplus food — so she just dumped all of this stuff on us and I can always remember Thanksgiving and Christmas we had a lot of food…
